problem:
Consider the function $f(x),$ defined as follows:

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}+{x}^{2}+x, & x\le 1 \\ x+a, & 1<x<3 \\ {x}^{2}-2x, & x\ge 3\end{aligned}
$$

Earlier part 1:

It is known that $f$ is continuous at $x=1.$ Find the value of $a.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $a=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        $e+1$

Earlier part 2:

${lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{x}^{3}+2}{f(x)}=$

                            
                                    
                            
                                        $\frac{3}{e+2}$

Current part:

Consider the part of $f(x)$ that's defined on the interval $x\in [3,c],$ where $c>3.$ Calculate the value of $c$ such that the average rate of change over $[3,c]$ is equal to $6.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $c=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}

feedback.worked_solution:
In part 1, we found that ${lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)=e+2\ne 0.$

Applying the quotient rule for limits, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{x}^{3}+2}{f(x)} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to 1}{x}^{3}+2}{{lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{3}+2}{e+2} \\  & =\frac{3}{e+2}.\end{aligned}
$$
